queer_characters.name: Lara Verhaeghen
queer_characters.notes: Lara is explicitly a 15-year-old transgender girl undergoing transition. Reception is split: 83% RT praise for poignant drama, but trans critics condemned exploitative framing (camera dwelling on her crotch, focus on breasts/vagina) and the self-mutilation scene as 'trans trauma porn,' while the real-life inspiration Nora Monsecour defended it as authentic to her experience.
queer_characters.contest_notes: Rep quality is genuinely disputed: trans critics (Rodriguez, Brennan, Whitney) call it dangerous and exploitative, while Monsecour, the trans dancer who inspired it, defends it as authentic and says the self-harm was crucial to depict as metaphor for suicidal ideation.

queer_creators.name: Nora Monsecour
queer_creators.notes: Trans Belgian dancer who inspired the film and collaborated on the project (uncredited). Exact production role is unclear from the source; listed here to credit her involvement, pending maintainer correction.

contributor_notes: Lara is played by Victor Polster, a cisgender male, chosen after gender-neutral casting; this casting choice was a major point of criticism. Director Lukas Dhont's identity is not stated in the source. Nora Monsecour's production role is ambiguous ('collaborated uncredited') — please verify before publishing. rep_quality flagged contested per the source's explicit note. No subtitle/audio languages mentioned in source. The self-harm/genital mutilation scene is central and heavily criticized; suicide trigger reflects Monsecour's framing of it as suicidal-ideation metaphor.
